title: Stick-It v0.8.1 — One Place
tldr: Settings finally stopped living in six different places: account, appearance, sharing, privacy, sounds and shortcuts now share one roof. Notes get a quick done tick and a way to trim empty paper, and the board gets a tidy-up button.
highlights: One settings home for account, appearance, sharing, privacy and data, sounds, shortcuts and legal, with one Save and one Cancel.
Clean up: tidy what's on your screen or the whole canvas, never delete a thing, and undo it in one step.
A quick done tick beside the x on every note.
Fit paper to content, Rip off empty paper, and a quiet corner handle to resize a note.
Comments hang off the note like a clipped paper slip.
added: Control Center: one dialog with a left rail (tabs on phones) opened from the avatar, the gear or the keyboard button, each at its own section.
Sounds section with a sound-effects switch, a volume slider and a soft preview (the sound library itself comes later).
Searchable Shortcuts cheat-sheet made of small key caps.
Legal & About section inside the Control Center.
Clean up button in the top bar with 'Clean my screen' and 'Clean whole canvas', counts before you apply, and one undo.
Status slip at the foot of the canvas for syncing, loading photos or media, preparing a share and exporting.
Quick Mark done tick beside the x on notes and checklists.
Fit paper to content, Rip off empty paper (torn, cut or notebook edge) and Restore full paper in the note menu.
A subtle corner handle to resize a selected note.
Comment tab on the object's bottom edge ('Comments · 2') and a compact thread slip that hangs under it.
Legal pages written on a spiral-notebook page, in English and Hebrew, light and dark.
improved: Active Shares, comments and the username check use the Stick-It loader instead of plain text.
Your own comments show your own picture; the crown now sits on the avatar everywhere an avatar is large enough.
The email-updates row is one short line.
Account numbers and sign-ins are fetched only when you open a section that shows them.
The profile avatar and the sharing preview are only redrawn when the picture itself changes.
fixed: Typing in Bio (or Name) no longer rebuilds the profile picture.
Pasted text no longer arrives highlighted or a line too low.
Alphabet Soup no longer carries a strip of washi tape.
Comment layout: author, time and delete no longer compete with the comment's words.
limitations: The Control Center was checked against a local stand-in for the account service; it has not been used on the real project yet.
Other people's pictures do not appear next to their comments (only initials), by design.
Board switching and first sign-in still use the full-screen loader, because the page reloads.
The reduced-motion setting was not toggled in a browser and no screen reader was run.
Finished notes still count toward a board's object limit.

title: Stick-It v0.8.0 — Cut It Out
tldr: Photos can now be cut out right on your device, you can right-click the board to add things, and the corkboard gains receipts, tickets, postcards, photo strips and a bowl of alphabet soup.
highlights: Real on-device cutouts with a Cutout Maker (Erase, Restore, Refine) and sticker or mounted looks.
Right-click the board to add things.
Receipts, tickets, postcards and photo strips.
A Done pile for finished notes.
Quiet collaboration: presence, comments and review states.
added: On-device cutout engine and the Cutout Maker.
Receipt, Ticket, Postcard and Photo Strip objects.
Alphabet Soup (Premium, enforced by the server).
Right-click insertion menu and object menus.
Done pile, Focus Mode formatting strip, inline video, audio progress and resizing, draggable minimap.
improved: Boards with many photos use far less memory.
While one object is selected the rest of the board stays still.
fixed: A duplicated cutout now draws as soon as its copy exists.
Dragging a note no longer rebuilds the minimap on every move.
limitations: Cluttered scenes do not cut out cleanly.
Realtime presence has not been exercised against a real project yet.
Touch editing in the Cutout Maker has not been tried on a physical phone.
